64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. (3) The wire agrees: of 559 samples across 55 game-channel streams, field 1 is never NaN and every one of the 163 finite values lies inside +/-pi (max 3.0190), and 16 of 162 equal atan2(dir.y,dir.x) of a nearby 0x003D direction vector to float32 round-off, 33 within 0.05 rad, against a null model whose 95th percentile is 5. WHICH SIGN IS A LEFT TURN IS UNVERIFIED (121/189 and 106/169 -- real but weak); no left/right claim is made here. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER TEXT: 'field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples' was true of those twelve and false as a generalisation -- it is 1.0 in 433 of 559, with 105 at 0.425 and a tail down to 0.10133, which CORROBORATES studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md R3 (411/536 and 105 before the 2026-08-10 runs existed) rather than refuting it. The floor is the client's own send gate: it refuses to send below 0.1, and the observed minimum is 0.10133. CORPUS CAVEAT: 536 of the 559 are the harness clicking fixed window fractions, 22 are 2026-08-10 loopback (17 of them tape-loaded), and 1 is live -- so the FREQUENCIES describe our own driver, not a player. The name does not rest on them; it rests on the binary. UPSTREAM ldufr/Headquarter numbers ROTATE_PLAYER 0x0040 independently (GWCA has 0x003E, the known +2 drift); see PLAN.md 6.1 for its register row. Evidence: vault/captures/live/20260807T143055 conn :60935 msg 52 (field1 = 1.08214450 rad = 62.0026 deg, exactly atan2 of the (360.53,678.12) direction the three preceding 0x003D carry), and toolkit/authsrv/test_rotate.py, which re-measures the wire-side invariants every run.

10.name: SEND_MACHINE_SPEC
10.why: Builder 0x00491820 has ZERO call sites: it is registered as a connection-established CALLBACK ('push 0x491820' at 0x00491BD9 into the connection factory), guarded to run at most once per process by a four-dword zero test. Every field traces to a Windows API: ole32!CoCreateGuid (resolved by name) for the blob, KERNEL32!GetSystemInfo dwNumberOfProcessors, CPUID leaves 0 and 1 (vendor string; 'and ecx,0xfff' signature), ntdll!RtlGetVersion major/minor/build, GlobalMemoryStatusEx >>20 for MB, and a literal 0x9020 stored when d3d9.dll loads. The frame arithmetic closes to the byte: base -0x238, last field ends at base+0xF0 = 240, matching 'push 0xf0'. Wire checks that could have failed: field 9 == 36896 == 0x9020 exactly; field 5 decodes to a valid 12-byte CPUID vendor string in both sessions; the blob is a structurally valid RFC4122 v4 UUID in both draws and DIFFERS between sessions on the same machine, which kills the machine-fingerprint reading. Fire-and-forget: the client sends its next message in the same TCP flush without waiting. Fields 10/11 (adapter PCI vendor/device) are INFERRED, field 12 UNVERIFIED. Prior art: authsrv.py:111-114 already reads 0x000A/0x000B as the computer-info pair -- that is OUR reconstruction and corroborates nothing; what is new is the per-field API trace.

18.name: REQUEST_QUEST_INFO
18.why: Thunk 0x0091FC00, one caller 0x0080DE09 inside 0x0080DDD0, whose assert ChCliApi.cpp:4253 'context->challengeSortArray.Find(challenge)' sits 18 bytes before the send call IN THE SAME FUNCTION -- the client's word for the argument is 'challenge'. It is a FETCH, not a push: both callers (QuestTaskTracker, QuestChallenge) reach the sender only on the FAILURE branch of a description lookup (0x0080DBE0 = 'test byte [esi+4],1; jne; xor eax,eax; ret'), and the alternative branch is assert(false) at QuestTaskTracker.cpp:299. Reply seals it: GAME_SMSG 0x004C on the same connection in 30.7-61.5 ms with field 1 equal to the requested id, 16 of 16, carrying two encoded strings. Cross-check the corpus could have failed: every 0x003B with code 0x01 is followed by exactly one 0x0012 carrying that id and no other code ever is -- 5 for 5 in each session, both directions. Consider REQUEST_QUEST_DESCRIPTION as the narrower alternative; the reply is a description.

43.name: COMPASS_DRAW
43.why: OBSERVED for the mechanism, MEDIUM for the NAME, and the split is the point. Build 38797. THE MECHANISM: wrapper 0x00920230 writes the opcode as an immediate (0x0092024B `mov dword [ebp-0x50], 0x2b`) and asserts CharMsg.cpp:8129 `knotCount <= arrsize(message.knotData)` @0x00920262. That first dword is called `messageId` by the client itself -- SendMessage 0x007DCF00 passes it to 0x007DDE00, whose first assert is MsgChannel.cpp:392 `messageId < channel->m_sendMsgs.Count()` @0x007DDE15, indexing an 8-byte-per-id descriptor array, and 0x007DCFCA `or ax, cx` is where the 0x8000 game-channel stamp is applied. SOLE PRODUCER IMAGE-WIDE, established twice by methods that share no premise. (1) The wrapper has exactly ONE direct reference, thunk 0x00816110, which has exactly ONE caller, 0x008C08DC, and neither VA occurs as a stored dword at any alignment in ANY of the five sections -- so neither is in a vtable, and not even a runtime-built table could hold one, since the store's immediate would itself be in .text. (2) A value-first sweep that cannot desync: of 134 materialisations of 0x2b in .text across six encodings, exactly ONE instruction sits inside the body of a function that calls a send entry -- 0x0092024B -- swept over all 214 send call sites, which is the CORRECTED census (there are TWO send entries, 0x007DCF00 and the dword-array variant 0x007DCB10 with 40 sites of its own; the earlier 174 missed the second). Controls on 0x78/0x39/0x3d/0x2c/0x40 each find their producer, and 0x40 surfaces six candidates that separate on which slot the buffer's `lea` names, so the method CAN report a second one. Reachability of the call site was tested rather than assumed: reverse closure over 135,455 direct call edges from the enclosing function 0x008C0840 converges at depth 25 on NINE functions, all inside 0x008BA79D..0x008C0840, no Gm* module anywhere. FIELD 1 IS A CLIENT-ALLOCATED STROKE HANDLE, not a target and not an agent: it is [canvas+0xbc], written at 0x008C0065 either by popping the back of a recycle pool at [canvas+0x68] or from the post-increment counter at [canvas+0x98], and the client looks its OWN line up with the key {0, that handle} at 0x008BF427-0x008BF442. Two wire facts corroborate the allocator and rule out a colour or ping-type reading: our corpus emits 7 then 6 (a DECREASING pair no plain counter produces), and two flushes 250 ms apart that are one stroke SHARE id 6 while two separate strokes 250 ms apart differ. A server must ECHO it in GAME_SMSG 0x0091 field 2, never invent it. FIELD 2 IS A POLYLINE IN TERRAIN CELLS. Each u32 packs two SIGNED int16, LOW HALF = x: the pack is 0x00920280-0x00920291, and the encoder at 0x008C07F0 divides each world float by the double 96.0 at 0x0094DE10 -- the terrain cell pitch -- AFTER 0x008C0560 has added the player's own world position, so the value is ABSOLUTE world/96 and not an offset. The receive side multiplies by that same constant at three sites (0x008BF177, 0x008BE6C7, 0x008BE774) and sign-extends both halves with movsx at 0x0091EA60/0x0091EA67. THE WIRE DISCRIMINATES ALL OF THAT and could have refuted it: the client's own constants bound a compass click at sqrt(0.1650390625) * 11076.9228515625 = 4500.0 world units exactly (hit test 0x008C0130 vs the world scale 0x00BA0318), and the corpus's one live sample -- 20260807T143055 conn :60935 t=50.702, `[32811, 7, [3801175]]`, knot 0x003A0057 -- lands at (8352, 5568), 3236.4 units from the position the preceding 0x003D reports 150 ms earlier and 5.0 degrees off that message's own heading, while the three rivals (halves swapped 7140.1, unscaled 11562.4, unscaled+swapped 11580.7) are all OUTSIDE the compass. Eight further knots in vault/captures/authsrv/authsrv-20260805T214038-c2.jsonl carry a NEGATIVE low half, which under an unsigned read would sit 6.29e6 units away. RATE: knots accumulate at a 25 ms floor (0x008BF45E `cmp ecx,0x19`, and a faster sample UPDATES the last knot in place) and flush on a 250 MILLISECOND countdown (0x008C08B8 `mov eax,0xfa`), sending nothing when empty -- so a drag is at most 10 knots per message and the 16 cap is never approached. The unit is milliseconds on three witnesses: the clock is WINMM!timeGetTime (import at 0x009396F8 via 0x0046B4E0 -> 0x0047F730), the same delta is divided by the literal 1000.0 at 0x008C0877, and OUR OWN CAPTURES show consecutive flushes of one stroke at 0.251988 s and 0.249950 s. A single knot is a click (a ping), a run is a drag. WHY THE NAME IS ONLY MEDIUM: the SEND side names nothing but `knotCount` and `message.knotData`. The word DRAW is ArenaNet's but lives only on the RECEIVE side, in GAME_SMSG 0x0091's bound constant CHAR_MAX_DRAW_MINIMAP_KNOT_COUNT, and reaches this opcode by INHERITANCE through the descriptor pairing (0x2b's SEND cmds and 0x91's RECV cmds are identical but for one leading u16). `PING` is not the client's word for anything -- 0 hits across all 19,758 readable asserts -- so it is GWW's player-facing vocabulary and is deliberately not used here. Two rivals were taken seriously and refuted: hero-flag placement (CompassCanvas.cpp does carry :416 and :902 `aiFlag < AI_COMMAND_FLAGS`, but that path reaches NO send entry, and a flag order is one point where this is 1-16 packed pairs rendered as a polyline gated on `knotCount >= 2`) and target call (no agent id anywhere; the u32 comes out of a free list, and the client types it 0x404 rather than with its type-0 agent_id tag). NOTE the naming hazard: GAME_SMSG 0x002B is a DIFFERENT message, already named AGENT_UPDATE_SPEED, with 309 live occurrences -- any census not split by direction is wrong by two orders of magnitude. Evidence: 1 live c2s occurrence, 5 in vault/captures/gamesrv|authsrv as kind:"decoded" with name "?" (dated 2026-08-14; that tree is append-only and two of the five are from this arc's own working day), and studies/minimap/FINDINGS.md 4.1.

421.why: Our table stops one field short AND mismarks the message variable. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00c01b70 (file 0x800b70) is [0x000001a5, 0x00001805, 0x00000404, 0x00000104, 0x00000204, 0x00000104, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bcb36c (file 0x7ca36c) statically holds count=8 and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 8 dwords later. Initializer at VA 0x004661d0-0x00466216 copies the statically-present constants [0x00c015a8]=0x1805, [0x00c015ac]=0x404, [0x00c01668]=0x104, [0x00c015dc]=0x204, [0x00c015e4]=0x104, [0x00c01520]=0x404, [0x00c0152c]=0x104. The final 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a trailing `byte` we do not have: 39 bytes, not 38. No type 7/11/12 field is present, so the message is FIXED, not variable_length.NAMED 2026-08-10, and it is the FIRST name any GAME_SMSG opcode has carried -- the imported catalog has field layouts for 487 of them and names for none. This one is earned the same way the seven GAME_CMSG names were: from a witness that was not consulted to make the claim. It is the GAME-channel twin of AUTH_SMSG 0x0009 GAME_SERVER_INFO. Field 1 is a sockaddr_in for the next instance (family u16 LE, port u16 BE, IPv4 -- the mixed endianness is the client's, and reading the port the other way round is a documented past failure), and fields 2, 4 and 6 are the next instance's world_id, map_id and player_id. EVIDENCE: across the three transitions in one recorded session, every one of those four values equals what the NEXT connection then sent in its own client-to-server VERSION frame -- 12 of 12 fields, parsed straight off wire.jsonl, which the decrypted channel files do not even carry. toolkit/authsrv/tape.py's chain() re-derives that every run and REFUSES a link it cannot prove, rather than ordering hops by timestamp. THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE and must not be: world_id and player_id are live session identifiers from the owner's own account, schema/ is tracked and the vault is not. Field 5 (offset +33) was 1, 0, 1 across the three hops, correlating with destination map 146/164/146 -- possibly an is-explorable flag, UNVERIFIED at n=3 with two of the three being the same map, so it stays unnamed. The 39-byte length this entry corrects is now CORROBORATED by ArenaNet's own stream as well as by the client's tables: in all three tapes the next message begins exactly 39 bytes later.
